entry.title: Why Does A-Shares Always End Up Paying the Bill?
entry.content: Why Does China’s A-Share Market Always Seem to Pay the Bill? Whenever war breaks out somewhere, the dollar strengthens, oil spikes, or U.S. stocks tumble, Chinese investors repeat a familiar line: A-shares are paying the bill again. That phrase survives because it matches lived experience. Middle East tensions rise, A-shares fall first. The Fed turns more hawkish, A-shares wobble. U.S. markets rally, A-shares may not follow. U.S. markets sell off, A-shares usually cannot hide. Over time, investors compress all of this into one brutal conclusion: whenever the world gets messy, A-shares settle the tab. That conclusion is not fully precise—but it is not mere whining either. A more accurate version would be this: A-shares are not destined to pay for every global shock, but they are one of the few major markets that habitually treat themselves as the first payer. This is not just about fundamentals. It is about capital structure, confidence structure, and narrative structure. 1. A-shares often respond with a discount first, analysis later In mature markets, external shocks are often sorted quickly: Which industries are directly hurt? Which assets actually benefit? Which companies are merely being sold on emotion? Which sectors have defensive qualities? A-shares eventually does this too—but often not in the first move. The first move in A-shares is often simpler: External risk is rising. Risk appetite is shrinking. Sell first. So the market’s initial reaction is frequently not “price winners and losers precisely,” but “mark down broad risk exposure first.” That is why investors so often feel that while other markets are still thinking, A-shares has already started paying. 2. The first root cause: the capital base is structurally more fragile A-shares has a persistent structural issue: too much trading capital, too little stable long-duration capital. A market genuinely dominated by long-horizon capital tends to reprice risk. A market heavily influenced by short-cycle money, thematic money, and tactical capital tends to de-risk first and think later. That produces a collective reflex: the first question is not how much this matters, but whether it is safer to cut exposure immediately. Once that reflex exists, external shocks will naturally produce faster, rougher, more mechanical selloffs. 3. The second cause: A-shares trades risk appetite, not just earnings People like to explain markets with earnings, margins, and balance sheets. But A-shares’ short- and medium-term moves are driven by more than EPS. It also trades: policy expectations liquidity expectations risk appetite whether a narrative can stay alive whether institutions are willing to keep crowding into the same themes So war, oil shocks, a stronger dollar, or overseas volatility can hit A-share valuations quickly even before they materially hit company earnings. In other words, the market is often discounting not tomorrow’s profits, but this: How much uncertainty are investors still willing to bear? That is why a seemingly distant macro event can trigger a very immediate price reaction. 4. The third cause: foreign flows, domestic positioning, and self-fulfilling panic A-shares is also unusually prone to second-guessing other people’s trades—especially foreign capital. When foreign money flows out, the market quickly imagines a larger story: Is there a deeper macro problem? Is global money rotating back into dollars? Will RMB assets remain under pressure? Is there another leg down coming? Domestic money then de-risks in advance. That weakens the tape. A weaker tape validates fear. Fear triggers more selling. That creates a classic negative loop: It is not that fundamentals instantly collapsed. It is that everyone believes someone else will sell first. This is one of the defining mechanics of A-share panic. 5. The fourth cause: weak long-term faith in buying the dip Why do many investors feel U.S. equities are more resilient? Because deep down, that market still carries a powerful belief system: core assets can compound over time leaders possess global competitiveness innovation can keep generating future cash flow after a large drawdown, there will be real money willing to step in That does not make U.S. markets perfect. It simply means there is a deeper reservoir of belief that declines can create opportunity. A-shares has struggled to build an equally durable layer of conviction. Too many participants ask: Is there a second leg lower? Will policy disappoint again? Will foreign flows continue to leave? Will tomorrow bring another fresh negative catalyst? So A-shares does not lack temporary optimism—it lacks persistent trust. And without persistent trust, external shocks are far more likely to turn into broad doubt. 6. The fifth cause: A-shares has an almost unlimited supply of bearish explanations Chinese investors know this one by instinct: A-shares can explain almost anything as bearish. War escalates: risk appetite falls, bearish War cools: demand must be weak, bearish Oil rises: costs go up, bearish Oil falls: demand is soft, bearish U.S. stocks rally: capital leaves for overseas, bearish U.S. stocks fall: external risk spills over, bearish Each explanation sounds plausible in isolation. The problem is cumulative: when a market always has a ready-made bearish narrative, it becomes easier for emotion to dominate prices. That is how investors end up with a deep sense of asymmetry: Good news may not materialize, but bad news always seems to count. 7. Why does A-shares so often feel like it won’t rise when it should, but drops hard when it can? Because rising requires alignment. Falling often requires only uncertainty. For A-shares to stage a durable advance, many things often need to line up: macro conditions cannot be too weak policy must provide support foreign flows cannot turn hostile domestic institutions must be willing to add risk the leading narrative cannot break risk appetite must recover But for the market to fall, sometimes one thing is enough: a fresh source of uncertainty That asymmetry matters. A-shares often rises through coordination, but falls through instinct. 8. But the full picture is subtler: the index pays first, then capital reallocates internally If you only watch the index, the verdict is obvious: A-shares pays for everything. If you look deeper, the pattern is more nuanced: the index may kneel first, but not every sector dies with it. A more realistic script often looks like this: The index sells off. High-beta, high-valuation, foreign-favored sectors are hit first. Risk appetite contracts sharply. Capital then searches for whatever does not have to die with the tape. That is how internal reallocation happens: geopolitical tension boosts defense and gold higher oil supports energy and coal lower risk appetite favors utilities and dividend names external pressure strengthens self-reliance and security themes So the problem is not that A-shares never offers opportunity. It is that opportunity often emerges only after the index has already priced fear. 9. Why is the phrase “A-shares pays the bill” so durable? Because it captures a real psychological truth: A-share investors often feel they are absorbing discounts generated by risks that are not fully their own. Those discounts are not always irrational. But they often arrive fast, hard, and without any feeling of fairness. From Middle East wars to the dollar cycle, from Treasury yields to global recession fears, the real impact on Chinese listed companies is often not zero—but also not catastrophic enough to justify the violence of the tape. Yet the screen often tells a simpler story: sell first, shrink volume, slash risk assets. Over time, investors stop describing a market move and start describing a condition of existence: The world shakes, and I hurt first. That is why the phrase survives. 10. Conclusion: the real problem is not that A-shares sometimes pays—it is that it is too quick to volunteer If I had to end with one sharp sentence, it would be this: The most frustrating thing about A-shares is not that it occasionally pays for global risk, but that it often swipes the card before even checking who ran up the bill. That is not just a joke. It is a market temperament problem. A resilient market facing external shocks should first distinguish, then price, then exploit mispricing. A market lacking confidence, long-duration capital, and durable trust is more likely to discount first, defend first, and surrender first. So no, A-shares is not fated to be the world’s payer forever. But until its capital base, trust structure, and pricing mechanism are meaningfully strengthened, Chinese investors will probably keep repeating the same old line: A-shares paid the bill again. And most of the time, they will feel justified saying it. — Liu Ruyan

entry.title: I Fixed a Bug in OpenClaw Dreaming — The Regex That Broke the Memory System
entry.content: Background OpenClaw’s Dreaming feature (background memory consolidation) is an experimental capability designed to: Light Phase: Scan recent memory files, extract key content into the short-term recall store REM Phase: Deduplicate and cluster the recall store Deep Phase: For sufficiently rich recall, call the LLM to generate a deep summary, write to DREAMS.md, and optionally promote it to MEMORY.md Configured to run automatically at 04:00 daily (customizable). Sounds great. But in reality: enabling it had zero effect — no output whatsoever. Symptoms Dreaming config shows enabled: true, cron schedule is correct openclaw memory status shows recall store always empty: 0 entries · 0 promoted DREAMS.md never generated memory/.dreams/short-term-recall.json does not exist Gateway logs show no errors, only silent “No short-term recall candidates.” Investigation Layer 1: Suspect Plugin / Config Checked plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming — config path correct, frequency set to 0 4 * * *. /dreaming on and /dreaming status both respond normally. Config is fine. Layer 2: Suspect Recall Store Write Permissions Checked /home/opc/.openclaw/workspace/memory/.dreams/ — directory exists, permissions normal. Not a permission issue. Layer 3: Suspect Trigger Channel Manually injected __openclaw_memory_core_short_term_promotion_dream__ event into the main session. The Hook was called (DREAMING_HOOK_FIRED_UNMISTAKABLE appeared in logs), the Pipeline executed but returned executed: false. The trigger channel works — problem is inside the pipeline. Layer 4: Suspect Recall Store Content Checked recall store: short-term-recall.json exists but entryCount: 0. Checked memory file list — canonical daily files stopped existing after 2026-04-04: memory/2026-04-03.md ✅ Last standard file memory/2026-04-04-x-credentials.md ❌ (not YYYY-MM-DD) memory/2026-04-07-title-copy.md ❌ (not YYYY-MM-DD) Checked session hook logs: OpenClaw’s built-in hooks/session-memory writes session fragment files in YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.md format, not the YYYY-MM-DD.md format Dreaming requires. Layer 5: Deep Dive into Code Read the compiled dist files, found the key function isShortTermMemoryPath(): // Original regex (broken) const RE = /(?:^|\/)memory\/(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})\.md$/; This regex only matches memory/2026-04-03.md — completely fails to match memory/2026-04-07-title-copy.md. And recordShortTermRecalls() has the write condition: if (result.source !== "memory") return; if (!isShortTermMemoryPath(result.path)) return; // write to recall store ← skipped silently here Both conditions must pass to write. As long as the filename doesn’t match the regex, writes are silently skipped with no logs. Root Cause OpenClaw’s session-memory hook changed the memory file naming convention: from standard YYYY-MM-DD.md to YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.md (session fragments). But Dreaming’s short-term recall entry regex was still the old one — only matching the standard format. The resulting chain: session-memory writes YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.md → Dreaming regex doesn't match → recall store stays empty → REM phase has no input → Deep phase doesn't trigger → DREAMS.md never generated This is a classic “interface contract mismatch” bug: both modules work correctly in isolation, but their input/output formats don’t align. The Fix Modified the regex in short-term-promotion-G9ML8hkA.js: // Before const RE = /(?:^|\/)memory\/(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})\.md$/; // After const RE = /(?:^|\/)memory\/(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})(?:-.*)?\.md$/; (?:-.*)? matches an optional -suffix part (suffix can be -HHMM or -arbitrary-topic). Two additional minor improvements were made in dreaming-CnlsXIYM.js (nice-to-have): Trigger allowlist broadened: expanded from only accepting heartbeat to ["heartbeat", "system", "cron"] Telegram reminder text parsing: correctly extracts the raw event name from “A scheduled reminder has been triggered. The reminder content is: xxx” Validation After patching, manually injected a cron probe: Schedule: 2026-04-08T06:50:48.000Z (14:50:48 CST) Payload: __openclaw_memory_core_short_term_promotion_dream__ Result: DREAMING_HOOK_FIRED_UNMISTAKABLE >>> trigger=heartbeat bodyLen=... Executing pipeline... done (executed: false, success: true) executed: false is expected — the day’s recall store entries were insufficient (threshold ≥ 3), so LLM did not generate a summary. The Pipeline completed fully; it just needs more content accumulated. Dreaming is now end-to-end functional. Lessons Learned When encountering “silent failures”, go read the dist source code first, don’t guess. OpenClaw’s error handling is clean — it won’t volunteer errors, you have to trace the conditional branches yourself. Interface contract mismatch is a classic distributed systems bug. Both modules work, but formats don’t align. Recommended fix: add broader filename matching in isShortTermMemoryPath(), or make the session-memory hook write standard daily files by default. The params.trigger value in a Hook is not necessarily the original event type. When a cron-triggered event reaches the before_agent_reply hook, the trigger value is "heartbeat" not "cron" — this is OpenClaw’s internal event routing. On next upgrade, only one patch location needs checking: short-term-promotion-G9ML8hkA.js. The other two changes are nice-to-have and don’t affect core functionality. 「独断万古，恐怖如斯。」 — 如烟大帝, 2026-04-08, from a battle with regular expressions

entry.title: Metabase Connect to Oracle Autonomous Database using wallet
entry.content: Metabase deployed on Oracle Cloud Free Tier. using wallet Connect to free Oracle Autonomous Database Steps 1 download metabase wget https://downloads.metabase.com/v0.44.3/metabase.jar 2、run java -jar metabase.jar After running and exiting, you can see plugins in directory,We need to save the downloaded ojdbc driver in this directory. 3、download oracle jdbc driver from https://www.oracle.com/database/technologies/appdev/jdbc-downloads.html download ojdbc11-full.tar.gz Remember, be sure to download the ojdbcxx-full driver file, because we need not only ojdbc11.jar, also need oraclepki.jar, osdt_cert.jar and osdt_core.jar using wallet 4、run metabase with jvm parameters java -classpath ./plugins/oraclepki.jar:./plugins/osdt_cert.jar:./plugins/osdt_core.jar:. \ -Doracle.net.tns_admin=/data/instantclient_19_10/network/admin \ -Doracle.net.wallet_location="(SOURCE=(METHOD=file)(METHOD_DATA=(DIRECTORY=/data/instantclient_19_10/network/admin)))" \ -Doracle.net.ssl_server_dn_match=true -jar metabase.jar 参数： Doracle.net.tns_admin : instantclient directory Doracle.net.wallet_location : wallet file directory 5、Add Database Connect Open the tnsnames.ora file in the wallet package, and check the configuration of any one of high, low, and medium, and take the values: host service_name Metabase Config panel Add Oracle Database ，as the picture shows： Save config ！

entry.title: Python uses the yahoo_financials_stmt package to get stock financial data from Yahoo Finance
entry.content: It is difficult to find a free stock financial data interface now. Extracting financial data from Yahoo Finance may be the easiest method in the free solution. Since yahoo Finance canceled API support, you can only write your own crawler or use a third-party library, but yahoo occasionally Page changes and regional restrictions also cause great trouble for crawling data. This article introduces the yahoo_financials_stmt package I recently submitted to get stock financial data Project address：https://github.com/luckfu/yahoo_financials_stmt Usage： Install yahoo_financials_stmt pip install git+https://github.com/luckfu/yahoo_financials_stmt.git Get Financials data import datetime from yahoo_financials_stmt import YahooFinancialsStmt yfs = YahooFinancialsStmt() finances=yfs.get_financials('box') View Financials data import datetime from yahoo_financials_stmt import YahooFinancialsStmt yfs = YahooFinancialsStmt() finances.keys() 返回: dict_keys(['balance_annual', 'balance_quarterly', 'earnings_annual', 'earnings_quarterly', 'income_annual', 'income_quarterly', 'cashflow_annual', 'cashflow_quarterly']) balance annual finances['balance_annual']

entry.title: Where is the Bluetooth PAN in macOS Monterey？ 😡
entry.content: I have an old mac pro in my office. The operating system is big sur. It uses wifi to connect to the internal network and Bluetooth to connect to the external network of the mobile phone. Unfortunately, I recently upgraded Monterey and the Bluetooth network connection disappeared.Bluetooth PAN is missing macOS big sur，bluetooth connection to mobile phone network macOS Monterey，“connection to network” disappeared. More unfortunately, in order to test whether the problem was caused by upgrading to macOS Monterey, I also upgraded another mac air to Monterey, so all my computers could not connect to the Bluetooth network.

entry.title: Use the docker container as a virtual machine
entry.content: The last article mentioned that Oracle Cloud’s free and popular 4c24g VM.Standard.A1.Flex model is difficult to apply, but in actual use, there are still many traps in the Oracle Cloud free package. The following are some common situations: Free hosting is over quota, free storage is over quota, oc priority to stop the resource is this A1.Flex vps 。 Flex.A1 The optional operating system is only oracle linux v7 or v8 , if you like ubuntu…😭 When the operating system is broken, unlike general cloud service consoles that can restore the image, you can only reapply Using a container as a virtual machine is not in line with the original intention of container application deployment, but in view of the above problems, docker is used to create a container instead of a virtual machine in this article. Everything is operated in the virtual machine. When the system disaster is unrecoverable, just delete container and Create the container again. Deployment steps ssh Log in to the host 1、Install docker yum install docker 2、Dockerfile Writing Dockerfile FROM ubuntu:20.04 LABEL MAINTAINER="luckfu.com" USER root # change root password to `ubuntu` RUN echo 'root:ubuntu' | chpasswd ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND noninteractive # install ssh server RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \ openssh-server sudo \ && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \ && mkdir -p /run/sshd \ && ssh-keygen -A \ && sed -i 's/#PermitRootLogin prohibit-password/PermitRootLogin yes/g' /etc/ssh/sshd_config \ && apt-get purge -y --auto-remove EXPOSE 22 # run ssh server CMD ["/usr/sbin/sshd", "-D", "-o", "ListenAddress=0.0.0.0"] 3、Generate image docker build -f ./Dockerfile -t ubuntu-ssh docker images view image list docker images REPOSITORY TAG IMAGE ID CREATED SIZE ubuntuos-ssh latest b6010c26ebb7 1 days ago 189MB ubuntu 20.04 d5ca7a445605 8 weeks ago 65.6MB 4、Launching containers 执行命令 docker run -d -p 9022:22 -p 8000-9000:8000-9000 \ -v /data/:/data \ --name ubuntuos-ssh ubuntuos-ssh parameters and meaning： Parameters Description -d Daemon mode -p Port Mapping [host port:Port in container] -v volume mapping [host vol:container vol] –name container name ubuntu-ssh In the above command, we deployed a container named ubuntuos-ssh, and set the host’s /data (you can apply for 100G “always free” storage in the oracle cloud and mount it to the host /data) is mounted under the /data of the container, and 9022 of the host is mapped to port 22 of the ssh service of the container, and ports 8000-9000 are opened for spare Check if the container is running CONTAINER ID IMAGE COMMAND CREATED STATUS PORTS NAMES 0c9cf191daf2 ubuntuos-ssh "/usr/sbin/sshd -D -…" 12 days ago Up 12 days 0.0.0.0:8000-9000->8000-9000/tcp, :::8000-9000->8000-9000/tcp, 0.0.0.0:9022->22/tcp, :::9022->22/tcp ubuntuos-ssh Log in to the container use ssh instead of exec -it to enter password: ubuntu ssh root@localhost -p 9022 root@localhost's password: (base) root@xxxxxxx:~# If login success, the container is running normally 5、Login from internet Login to Oracle Cloud Check VNC config ,port 22 8000-9000 used by the container is open checks the firewall such as iptables firwwall，port is open ssh root@IP -p 9022 Let’s play

entry.title: Use python scripts to preemptively create Oracle VM.Standard.A1.Flex
entry.content: Oracle cloud open registered account can apply for 4c24g free cloud server, database and other services, 1c1g x86 server is easier to apply, but the popular 4c24g Ampere A1 type of host under normal circumstances can not apply through the web, currently popular on the Internet Cybersquatting methods are nothing more than two modes： Browser plug-ins or scripts or button wizards. The problem with this method is that the console is timed out. It is also easy to be judged by the server as illegal operations. Accounts are disabled. It is obviously not suitable for operations that require stable operation for several days. Call the oci command script, this is the safest mode, because oci is officially provided by oracle, the principle is to use the oci command to directly apply for an instance, for example： oci compute instance launch .... However, according to my Hong Kong host test, this can only be refreshed every 20 seconds at most, because the complete process of the oci command execution： 1、start to connect to oracle cloud 2、Verify user legitimacy 3、Excuting an command 4、exit Steps 1, 2, and 4 waste a lot of time in the loop. In this article, we use python to call the oci api , omit multiple verification , and execute the create instance command in loop. The refresh speed can reach 3 seconds/time. When the instance creation is successful, return ,Automatic withdrawal. Deployment steps 1、Download oci tools bash -c "$(curl –L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oracle/oci-cli/master/scripts/install/install.sh)" By default, press Enter. After the installation is complete, execute the following command to check whether it is successful oci -v 2、Configure oci On the oracle cloud console, click on the avatar in the upper right corner => select “User Settings” in the menu to copy the user and tenancy OCID execute oci setup config Fill in the correct user and tenancy id Enter a location for your config [/root/.oci/config]: Enter a user OCID: #your user ocid Enter a tenancy OCID: #your tenancy ocid Enter a region by index or name(e.g. 1: ap-chiyoda-1, 2: ap-chuncheon-1, 3: ap-hyderabad-1, 4: ap-melbourne-1, 5: ap-mumbai-1, 6: ap-osaka-1, 7: ap-seoul-1, 8: ap-sydney-1, 9: ap-tokyo-1, 10: ca-montreal-1, 11: ca-toronto-1, 12: eu-amsterdam-1, 13: eu-frankfurt-1, 14: eu-zurich-1, 15: me-dubai-1, 16: me-jeddah-1, 17: sa-santiago-1, 18: sa-saopaulo-1, 19: uk-cardiff-1, 20: uk-gov-cardiff-1, 21: uk-gov-london-1, 22: uk-london-1, 23: us-ashburn-1, 24: us-gov-ashburn-1, 25: us-gov-chicago-1, 26: us-gov-phoenix-1, 27: us-langley-1, 28: us-luke-1, 29: us-phoenix-1, 30: us-sanjose-1): 9 # select you regist region Do you want to generate a new API Signing RSA key pair? (If you decline you will be asked to supply the path to an existing key.) [Y/n]: y #y Enter a directory for your keys to be created [/root/.oci]: Enter a name for your key [oci_api_key]: Public key written to: /root/.oci/oci_api_key_public.pem Enter a passphrase for your private key (empty for no passphrase): Private key written to: /root/.oci/oci_api_key.pem Fingerprint: Config written to /root/.oci/config ... Copy the generated public key and get the command as follows： cat /root/.oci/oci_api_key_public.pem Copy the displayed content. And add it to Identity=>Users=>User Details=>API Keys Key»Add API Keys 3、python programe Install python oci Assuming you have installed the python environment pip install oci Login public certificate Create a new or use the existing certificate of the system, this article directly check the existing certificate of this machine and record it cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAA......local Modify script download: link Modify the parameters in the luanch.py ​​script INSTANCE_NAME = 'apply instance name' #If you are a new user, create a VCN first SUBNET_ID = "Networking=>Virtual Cloud Networks=>Virtual Cloud Network Details OCID" compartment_id= "tenancy OCID" ssh_public_key="Contents of id_rsa.pub" run script Execute the script, when the instance apply completed, it will automatically exit python ./luanch.py

entry.title: About
entry.content: Written in Go, Hugo is an open source static site generator available under the Apache Licence 2.0. Hugo supports TOML, YAML and JSON data file types, Markdown and HTML content files and uses shortcodes to add rich content. Other notable features are taxonomies, multilingual mode, image processing, custom output formats, HTML/CSS/JS minification and support for Sass SCSS workflows. Hugo makes use of a variety of open source projects including: https://github.com/yuin/goldmark https://github.com/alecthomas/chroma https://github.com/muesli/smartcrop https://github.com/spf13/cobra https://github.com/spf13/viper Hugo is ideal for blogs, corporate websites, creative portfolios, online magazines, single page applications or even a website with thousands of pages. Hugo is for people who want to hand code their own website without worrying about setting up complicated runtimes, dependencies and databases. Websites built with Hugo are extremely fast, secure and can be deployed anywhere including, AWS, GitHub Pages, Heroku, Netlify and any other hosting provider. Learn more and contribute on GitHub.
